  (\lean{ErgodicTheory.uCover}) lap by lap on the strip. Across one fundamental-domain seam --- the
  identification \([T x, s] = [x, s + c]\) --- the candidate is unchanged, because the base jump
  \(u_0(T x) - u_0(x)\) is \emph{precisely} the lap integral \(\int_0^{c} F([x,\sigma])\,d\sigma\)
  that the fibre integral accumulates over one roof height.
\end{lemma}

n33730.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{def:livsic-induced}
  The base cohomological equation \(\texttt{inducedBaseCocycle}\,F\,x = u_0(T x) - u_0(x)\) supplies
  the value of the seam jump; with a constant roof the one-lap integral \(\int_0^{\tau x}F([x,\sigma])
  \,d\sigma = \int_0^{c}F([x,\sigma])\,d\sigma\) is exactly this jump, so the two descriptions of
  \(\texttt{uCover}\) across the seam agree by interval-integral additivity. No estimate; a pure
  identity. Its upgrade to full \(\mathbb{Z}\)-invariance under the suspension action is
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.uCover_act}.
\end{proof}

n33731.title: Tier-III equivalence for constant-roof suspension flows

n33733.title: Flow-native form

n33735.title: Flow-Livšic for the cat-map suspension flow

n33737.title: Non-vacuity of the coboundary side
n33737.content:
\begin{theorem}[Non-vacuity of the coboundary side]\label{isFlowCoboundary_sinFibreObservable}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.CatMapToral.isFlowCoboundary_sinFibreObservable}\leanok
  \uses{livsic_catSuspensionFlow}
  A \(1\)-periodic fibre profile \(h\) descends to a flow observable \(F[x,s] = h(s)\) on the cat
  suspension (\lean{ErgodicTheory.CatMapToral.fibreObservable}, a \(\texttt{Quotient.lift}\) whose
  well-definedness is the profile's periodicity). For the concrete choice \(h(s) = \sin(2\pi s)\)
  (\lean{ErgodicTheory.CatMapToral.sinFibreObservable}), the induced base observable vanishes
  identically --- its one-lap integral is \(\int_0^{1}\sin(2\pi s)\,ds = 0\) --- so all periodic
  sums vanish and \(\texttt{sinFibreObservable}\) \emph{is} a flow coboundary of the cat-map
  suspension flow.
\end{theorem}

n33738.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{livsic_catSuspensionFlow}
  The one-lap integral \(\int_0^{1}\sin(2\pi s)\,ds = 0\) makes \(\texttt{inducedBaseCocycle}\,F\)
  identically zero, so its periodic Birkhoff sums vanish trivially; the backward direction of
  \Cref{livsic_catSuspensionFlow} supplies the flow transfer function. Together with the obstruction
  witness \(F = 1\) (\Cref{thm:livsic-cat-suspension}), this certifies the tier-III equivalence is
  non-vacuous on both sides --- some observables cobound, others do not.
\end{proof}

n33739.title: Hölder flow coboundary

n33740.title: The induced base observable is Hölder

n33741.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{def:livsic-induced}
  The one-lap integral \(\int_0^{1} F[x, \sigma]\,d\sigma\) inherits the embedding-Hölder modulus of
  \(F\); the base distance \(d(x, y)\) is recovered from the embedding metric through the two
  Kuratowski test bundles \(\operatorname{muFun}/\operatorname{nuFun}\) (a \(2\times 2\) elimination)
  and, in the seam-wrap regime, through \(\operatorname{dist\_map\_le\_embDist\_wrap}\), while
  Lipschitz continuity of \(T\) controls the \(d(Tx, Ty)\) term.
\end{proof}

n33742.title: Cross-seam Hölder gluing

n33743.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{holderWith_inducedBaseCocycle, uCover_gen}
  Following the exact-seam philosophy of \Cref{uCover_gen}: on the fundamental strip the fibre
  integral is controlled by the embedding-Hölder modulus of \(F\), the base value by the discrete
  Hölder transfer \(u_0\), and the seam is bridged by two algebraically equivalent (from-below and
  from-above) representations of \(\operatorname{uCover}\), matched by the base cohomological identity
  \(\operatorname{inducedBaseCocycle} F\,x = u_0(Tx) - u_0(x)\). The base-distance recoveries reuse
  the two Kuratowski bundles and the seam-wrap primitive.
\end{proof}

n33744.title: Hölder flow-Livšic, constant roof
n33744.content:
\begin{theorem}[Hölder flow-Livšic, constant roof]\label{livsic_holderFlow_constRoof}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.livsic_holderFlow_constRoof}\leanok
  \uses{IsHolderFlowCoboundary, holderWith_suspTransfer, thm:livsic-induced-cob, def:livsic-expclosing}
  Let \(T\) be a Lipschitz homeomorphism of a compact metric base with \(\operatorname{diam} X\le 1\),
  the summed exponential closing property and a dense forward orbit, and let \(F\) be an
  \(\operatorname{embDist}\)-\(r\)-Hölder (\(0 < r\le 1\)), bounded flow observable with per-fibre
  interval-integrable restrictions. Then
  \[
    F \text{ is a Hölder flow coboundary of } \zeta
      \iff \operatorname{inducedBaseCocycle} T\,\tau\,F \text{ has vanishing periodic sums,}
  \]
  the flow-native (closed-orbit) form being
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.livsic_holderFlow_constRoof_orbitIntegral}. This is simultaneously tier 2 (the
  Hölder-regularity upgrade) and the issue's tier-4 Anosov statement over the suspension presentation.
\end{theorem}

n33745.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{holderWith_suspTransfer, thm:livsic-induced-cob}
  Forward: a Hölder flow coboundary is a flow coboundary, which induces a base coboundary
  (\Cref{thm:livsic-induced-cob}) with vanishing periodic sums (\Cref{thm:livsic-trivial}). Backward:
  vanishing periodic sums feed the base Hölder-Livšic converse (\Cref{thm:livsic-existence}, applied to
  the Hölder induced observable \Cref{holderWith_inducedBaseCocycle}) to produce a Hölder base transfer
  \(u_0\); the cross-seam gluing \Cref{holderWith_suspTransfer} makes the fundamental-domain candidate
  \(\operatorname{embDist}\)-Hölder and seam-invariant, so it descends to a genuine Hölder flow transfer
  function.
\end{proof}

n33746.title: Hölder flow-Livšic, variable Lipschitz roof

n33747.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{livsic_holderFlow_constRoof}
  Repeat the constant-roof argument on the normalized fibre coordinate. The metric compares points at
  normalized heights \(u = s/\tau x\) while the transfer integrates raw heights; the change of variables
  \(\sigma = \tau x\cdot w\) puts both fibre integrands at a common normalized height and lets the
  variable-roof horizontal-length bound control the fibre difference. The general-roof seam identity
  (\lean{ErgodicTheory.uCover_gen_var}, seam at height \(\tau x\)) glues the candidate; \emph{Lipschitz}
  continuity of \(\tau\) is essential --- the fibre-comparison factor \(\left\lvert \tau x - \tau y \right\rvert\) stays at
  exponent \(1\), so the assembled transfer keeps exponent \(r\); a merely \(r\)-Hölder roof would
  degrade it to \(r^2\) (disclosed, not delivered).
\end{proof}

n33748.title: Hölder flow-Livšic for the cat-map suspension flow

n33749.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{livsic_holderFlow_constRoof, thm:livsic-cat}
  Instantiate \Cref{livsic_holderFlow_constRoof} at the cat map: the diameter bound
  \(\operatorname{diam}\mathbb{T}^2\le 1\) (\lean{ErgodicTheory.CatMapToral.catTorus_dist_le_one}), the
  \(3\)-Lipschitz constant (\lean{ErgodicTheory.CatMapToral.lipschitzWith_catTorus}), continuity, the
  Anosov summed closing (\Cref{thm:livsic-cat-closing}) and the ergodic dense orbit
  (\Cref{thm:livsic-ergodic-dense}) discharge every base hypothesis.
\end{proof}

n33750.title: Non-vacuity on both sides
n33750.content:
\begin{theorem}[Non-vacuity on both sides]\label{isHolderFlowCoboundary_sinFibreObservable}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.CatMapToral.isHolderFlowCoboundary_sinFibreObservable}\leanok
  \uses{livsic_catSuspensionHolderFlow, thm:livsic-cat-suspension}
  The equivalence has content on both sides. The \(\sin(2\pi\cdot)\) fibre profile
  \(\operatorname{sinFibreObservable}\) is embedding-Hölder and \emph{is} a Hölder flow coboundary of
  the cat suspension (its one-lap integral \(\int_0^{1}\sin(2\pi s)\,ds = 0\) makes the induced base
  observable vanish); by contrast the constant observable \(1\) is embedding-Hölder yet \emph{not} a
  Hölder flow coboundary
  (\lean{ErgodicTheory.CatMapToral.const_one_not_isHolderFlowCoboundary_catSuspension}), since a Hölder
  flow coboundary is in particular a flow coboundary and \(1\) is defeated by the closed-orbit
  obstruction \Cref{thm:livsic-cat-suspension}.
\end{theorem}

n33751.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{livsic_catSuspensionHolderFlow, thm:livsic-cat-suspension}
  Coboundary side: \(\int_0^1\sin(2\pi s)\,ds = 0\) gives vanishing periodic sums, so the backward
  direction of \Cref{livsic_catSuspensionHolderFlow} supplies the Hölder flow transfer. Obstruction
  side: \(\operatorname{IsHolderFlowCoboundary.isFlowCoboundary}\) reduces to
  \Cref{thm:livsic-cat-suspension}, where the period-\(1\) fixed point charges the single lap integral
  \(1\ne 0\).
\end{proof}

n33752.title: Density matrix
n33752.content:
\begin{definition}[Density matrix]\label{DensityMatrix}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.DensityMatrix}\leanok
  For a finite index type \(n\), a \emph{density matrix} is a structure bundling a matrix
  \(\rho\in\operatorname{Matrix}_n(\mathbb{C})\) together with proofs that \(\rho\) is positive semidefinite and has
  unit trace, \(\Tr\rho = 1\). It is the finite-dimensional state of a quantum system on
  \(\mathbb{C}^n\).
\end{definition}

n33753.title: Eigenvalues form a probability vector

n33754.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{DensityMatrix}
  Positive semidefiniteness gives \(\lambda_i\ge 0\). The Hermitian spectral theorem identifies
  \(\Tr\rho\) with \(\sum_i\lambda_i\) as a complex number; casting the hypothesis \(\Tr\rho = 1\)
  back to \(\mathbb{R}\) yields \(\sum_i\lambda_i = 1\). Each \(\lambda_i\le 1\) is then a single term
  bounded by the sum of the nonnegative terms.
\end{proof}

n33755.title: Von Neumann entropy

n33756.title: Nonnegativity of entropy

n33758.title: Right partial trace
n33758.content:
\begin{definition}[Right partial trace]\label{partialTraceRight}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.partialTraceRight}\leanok
  For an operator \(M\) on a bipartite system \(\mathbb{C}^{n_A}\otimes\mathbb{C}^{n_B}\), the \emph{partial
  trace over the \(B\) factor} is
  \[
    (\Tr_B M)_{i,i'} \;=\; \sum_j M_{(i,j),(i',j)},
  \]
  an operator on \(\mathbb{C}^{n_A}\). (The left partial trace \(\Tr_A\) is defined symmetrically.)
\end{definition}

n33759.title: Partial trace preserves the trace

n33761.title: Partial trace is completely positive

n33762.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{partialTraceRight}
  Write the partial trace in Kraus/compression form \(\Tr_B M = \sum_j E_j^{*} M E_j\), the sum
  of the conjugations of \(M\) by the block-inclusion isometries \(E_j : i\mapsto(i,j)\). Each
  compression \(E_j^{*} M E_j\) is positive semidefinite, and a finite sum of positive
  semidefinite matrices is positive semidefinite.
\end{proof}

n33763.title: Maximum-entropy Jensen bound
n33763.content:
\begin{lemma}[Maximum-entropy Jensen bound]\label{sum_negMulLog_le_log_card}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.sum_negMulLog_le_log_card}\leanok
  For a probability vector \(p\) supported on a nonempty finite set \(s\) (\(p_i\ge 0\) and
  \(\sum_{i\in s}p_i = 1\)), the entropy sum is bounded by the log-cardinality,
  \[
    \sum_{i\in s}\operatorname{negMulLog}(p_i) \;\le\; \log\left\lvert s \right\rvert,
  \]
  with equality at the uniform distribution \(p\equiv 1/\left\lvert s \right\rvert\).
\end{lemma}

n33764.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  The concave Jensen inequality (\(\texttt{ConcaveOn.le\_map\_sum}\)) for
  \(\operatorname{negMulLog}\) with the uniform weights \(w_i = \left\lvert s \right\rvert^{-1}\) gives
  \(\left\lvert s \right\rvert^{-1}\sum_i\operatorname{negMulLog}(p_i)\le\operatorname{negMulLog}\bigl(\left\lvert s \right\rvert^{-1}\sum_i p_i\bigr) = \operatorname{negMulLog}(\left\lvert s \right\rvert^{-1})\); evaluating
  \(\operatorname{negMulLog}(\left\lvert s \right\rvert^{-1}) = \left\lvert s \right\rvert^{-1}\log\left\lvert s \right\rvert\) and cancelling the positive
  factor \(\left\lvert s \right\rvert^{-1}\) gives the claim. This is factored out of both entropy layers so the single
  Jensen argument is not inlined twice.
\end{proof}

n33765.title: A state has positive rank

n33767.title: Maximum-entropy bound
n33767.content:
\begin{theorem}[Maximum-entropy bound]\label{vonNeumannEntropy_le_log_rank}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.vonNeumannEntropy_le_log_rank}\leanok
  The von Neumann entropy of a density matrix is at most the logarithm of its rank,
  \[
    S(\rho) \;\le\; \log\bigl(\operatorname{rank}\rho\bigr).
  \]
  Among all states supported on a \(k\)-dimensional subspace, the maximally mixed state --- with
  entropy \(\log k\) --- is the most disordered.
\end{theorem}

n33768.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{vonNeumannEntropy, sum_negMulLog_le_log_card, DensityMatrix.rank_pos}
  Restrict the entropy sum \(S(\rho) = \sum_i\operatorname{negMulLog}(\lambda_i)\) to the support
  \(s = \{i : \lambda_i\ne 0\}\); the off-support terms vanish because
  \(\operatorname{negMulLog}(0) = 0\), and the restricted eigenvalues still sum to \(1\). The support
  cardinality equals the rank (\(\texttt{IsHermitian.rank\_eq\_card\_non\_zero\_eigs}\)) and is
  positive (\Cref{DensityMatrix.rank_pos}), so the uniform-weight Jensen bound
  (\Cref{sum_negMulLog_le_log_card}) applied on \(s\) gives
  \(S(\rho)\le\log\left\lvert s \right\rvert = \log(\operatorname{rank}\rho)\).
\end{proof}

n33769.title: Bound by the ambient dimension

n33771.title: Strict positivity off the pure states

n33772.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{vonNeumannEntropy, vonNeumannEntropy_nonneg}
  Entropy is a sum of nonnegative terms (\Cref{vonNeumannEntropy_nonneg}), so \(S(\rho) = 0\) forces
  every \(\operatorname{negMulLog}(\lambda_i) = 0\); since each \(\lambda_i\in[0,1]\) this drives
  every eigenvalue to \(\{0,1\}\). A diagonal matrix with \(\{0,1\}\) entries is idempotent, and
  idempotency is transported through the spectral unitary (a \(*\)-algebra automorphism, hence
  multiplicative), yielding \(\rho^2 = \rho\) --- contradicting the hypothesis. Hence \(S(\rho) > 0\).
\end{proof}

n33773.title: Block-inclusion Kraus operators

n33774.title: Kraus conjugation is a block compression

n33776.title: Explicit Kraus form of the partial traces
n33776.content:
\begin{theorem}[Explicit Kraus form of the partial traces]\label{partialTraceRight_eq_kraus}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.partialTraceRight_eq_kraus,
    ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.partialTraceLeft_eq_kraus}\leanok
  \uses{partialTraceRight, krausInclusionRight, krausConjRight_eq_submatrix}
  Both partial traces are genuine sums of Kraus conjugations:
  \[
    \Tr_B M \;=\; \sum_{j\in n_B} E_j\,M\,E_j^{*},
    \qquad
    \Tr_A M \;=\; \sum_{i\in n_A} F_i\,M\,F_i^{*}.
  \]
  The left analogue is \texttt{partialTraceLeft\_eq\_kraus}.
\end{theorem}

n33778.title: Co-isometry of each block inclusion

n33780.title: Completeness relation
n33780.content:
\begin{lemma}[Completeness relation]\label{sum_conjTranspose_mul_krausInclusionRight}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.sum_conjTranspose_mul_krausInclusionRight,
    ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.sum_conjTranspose_mul_krausInclusionLeft}\leanok
  \uses{krausInclusionRight}
  The block inclusions satisfy the Kraus completeness / trace-preservation relation on the full
  \(A\otimes B\) space,
  \[
    \sum_{j\in n_B} E_j^{*}E_j \;=\; 1,
    \qquad
    \sum_{i\in n_A} F_i^{*}F_i \;=\; 1.
  \]
  The left analogue is \texttt{sum\_conjTranspose\_mul\_krausInclusionLeft}.
\end{lemma}

n33781.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{krausInclusionRight}
  \(\bigl(\sum_j E_j^{*}E_j\bigr)_{(p),(p')} = \sum_{a,j}[\,p = (a,j)\,][\,p' = (a,j)\,]
  = [\,p = p'\,]\), the identity on \(\mathbb{C}^{n_A\times n_B}\). This is a genuinely different identity
  from the co-isometry \Cref{krausInclusionRight_mul_conjTranspose}: summing that one instead gives
  \(\sum_j E_j E_j^{*} = \#n_B\cdot 1\), not \(1\).
\end{proof}

n33782.title: Umegaki relative entropy
n33782.content:
\begin{definition}[Umegaki relative entropy]\label{relEntropy}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.relEntropy}\leanok
  \uses{DensityMatrix}
  The \emph{Umegaki relative entropy} of \(\rho\) with respect to \(\sigma\) is
  \(S(\rho\|\sigma) = \Tr\rho(\log\rho - \log\sigma)\). It is defined in the concrete
  \emph{spectral/overlap} form
  \[
    S(\rho\|\sigma) \;=\; \sum_k p_k\log p_k \;-\; \sum_{k,m}\left\lvert \langle e_k\mid f_m\rangle \right\rvert^2\,
      p_k\log q_m,
  \]
  where \((p_k,e_k)\) are the eigenvalues/eigenvectors of \(\rho\) and \((q_m,f_m)\) those of
  \(\sigma\). The definition is total: with the convention \(\log 0 = 0\) the \(\sigma\)-singular
  columns contribute \(0\).
\end{definition}

n33783.title: Trace form of relative entropy
n33783.content:
\begin{theorem}[Trace form of relative entropy]\label{relEntropy_eq_traceLog}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.relEntropy_eq_traceLog}\leanok
  For faithful (positive definite) \(\sigma\), the spectral definition agrees with the textbook
  trace form
  \[
    S(\rho\|\sigma) \;=\; \Re\,\Tr\bigl(\rho\,(\log\rho - \log\sigma)\bigr),
  \]
  where \(\log\rho,\log\sigma\) are the Hermitian continuous functional calculus of the real
  logarithm.
\end{theorem}

n33784.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{relEntropy}
  Expand both eigendecompositions. The trace--spectral bridge
  \(\Re\,\Tr(\rho\,f(\tau)) = \sum_{k,m} p_k\left\lvert \langle e_k\mid g_m\rangle \right\rvert^2 f(q_m)\) (proved
  once, entrywise, via the spectral theorem and the identity \(z\bar z = \left\lvert z \right\rvert^2\)) identifies
  \(\Re\,\Tr(\rho\log\rho)\) with \(\sum_k p_k\log p_k\) (the overlap of \(\rho\) with itself is
  the identity) and \(\Re\,\Tr(\rho\log\sigma)\) with the cross double sum. Distributing over the
  difference gives the claim.
\end{proof}

n33785.title: Klein / Gibbs nonnegativity

n33786.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{relEntropy, DensityMatrix.sum_eigenvalues_eq_one, klein_scalar}
  The overlap matrix \(D_{km} = \left\lvert \langle e_k\mid f_m\rangle \right\rvert^2\) is doubly stochastic:
  writing \(Q = \rho.\mathrm{eigVec}^{*}\,\sigma.\mathrm{eigVec}\), both \(QQ^{*} = 1\) and
  \(Q^{*}Q = 1\) (the eigenvector unitaries cancel), giving unit row and column sums.
  Faithfulness makes every \(q_m > 0\), so the support side condition is vacuous. Klein's scalar
  inequality (\Cref{klein_scalar}) then yields
  \(\sum_{k,m} D_{km}\,p_k\log q_m \le \sum_k p_k\log p_k\), i.e.\ \(0\le S(\rho\|\sigma)\).
\end{proof}

n33787.title: Vanishing on the diagonal

n33789.title: Unitary invariance

n33790.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{relEntropy_eq_traceLog}
  Conjugation by \(W\) is a \(*\)-algebra automorphism, so it commutes with the functional
  calculus: \(\log(W\rho W^{*}) = W(\log\rho)W^{*}\). Hence each trace
  \(\Tr\bigl((W\rho W^{*})\log(W\tau W^{*})\bigr) = \Tr\bigl(W(\rho\log\tau)W^{*}\bigr)
  = \Tr(\rho\log\tau)\) by cyclicity of the trace and \(W^{*}W = 1\). Applying this to the two
  terms of the trace form leaves \(S(\rho\|\sigma)\) unchanged.
\end{proof}

n33791.title: Ancilla invariance

n33793.title: Scalar Klein / Peierls inequality
n33793.content:
\begin{theorem}[Scalar Klein / Peierls inequality]\label{klein_scalar}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.klein_scalar}\leanok
  Let \(D = (D_{km})\) be a doubly stochastic \(K\times M\) matrix (\(D_{km}\ge 0\), all row sums
  and all column sums equal to \(1\)), let \(p\ge 0\) on \(K\) and \(s\ge 0\) on \(M\) have equal
  total mass \(\sum_k p_k = \sum_m s_m\), and assume the support condition
  \(s_m = 0\Rightarrow D_{km}p_k = 0\). Writing \(a_m = \sum_k D_{km}p_k\) for the column
  marginal,
  \[
    \sum_m a_m\log s_m \;\le\; \sum_k p_k\log p_k.
  \]
\end{theorem}

n33794.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  This is the finite scalar core of Klein's inequality (Carlen, \emph{Trace Inequalities and
  Quantum Entropy}, Thm.~2.11; Peierls, Thm.~2.9). The termwise Peierls bound \(p - s\le p\log p - p\log s\) (valid for
  \(p\ge 0\), \(s > 0\), from \(\log(s/p)\le s/p - 1\)) is scaled by \(D_{km}\ge 0\) and summed
  over the double index. Double stochasticity makes the mass-balance term
  \(\sum_{k,m} D_{km}(p_k - s_m)\) telescope to \(\sum_k p_k - \sum_m s_m = 0\); the columns with
  \(s_m = 0\) contribute nothing by the support hypothesis (there \(a_m = 0\)). Rearranging the
  summed inequality yields the claim.
\end{proof}

n33795.title: Subadditivity of the von Neumann entropy
n33795.content:
\begin{theorem}[Subadditivity of the von Neumann entropy]\label{vonNeumannEntropy_subadditive}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.vonNeumannEntropy_subadditive}\leanok
  For a bipartite density matrix \(\rho\) on \(n_A\otimes n_B\) with reduced density matrices
  \(\rho_A = \Tr_B\rho\) and \(\rho_B = \Tr_A\rho\), the von Neumann entropy is subadditive:
  \[
    S(\rho) \;\le\; S(\rho_A) + S(\rho_B).
  \]
\end{theorem}

n33796.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{klein_scalar, vonNeumannEntropy, partialTraceRight}
  An elementary route through the scalar Klein inequality, with no matrix logarithm (Carlen,
  \emph{Trace Inequalities and Quantum Entropy}, Thm.~2.11; Nielsen--Chuang \S11.3). Diagonalize
  \(\rho = G\,\mathrm{diag}(p)\,G^{*}\), \(\rho_A = U\,\mathrm{diag}(\lambda)\,U^{*}\),
  \(\rho_B = V\,\mathrm{diag}(\mu)\,V^{*}\) and set \(Q = G^{*}(U\otimes V)\), a unitary. Then
  \(D_{km} = \left\lvert Q_{km} \right\rvert^2\) is doubly stochastic, and the conjugation--partial-trace identity
  \(\Tr_B\bigl((U\otimes V)^{*}\rho(U\otimes V)\bigr) = U^{*}(\Tr_B\rho)U\) (and its left analogue)
  identifies the marginals of \(D\) with \(\lambda\) and \(\mu\). Feeding \(D\), the eigenvalue
  vector \(p\), and the product vector \(s_{(i,j)} = \lambda_i\mu_j\) into \Cref{klein_scalar}
  gives \(\sum_i\eta(\lambda_i) + \sum_j\eta(\mu_j)\ge\sum_k\eta(p_k)\) (with \(\eta(t) = -t\log t\)),
  which is the assertion after negation.
\end{proof}

n33797.title: Operator convexity of \(-\log\)

n33798.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  Transport the statement along the \(\mathbb{R}\)-linear star-algebra equivalence
  \(\operatorname{Matrix}\simeq\texttt{CStarMatrix}\) (identity on the shared carrier, order- and
  cfc-preserving) onto the \(C^{*}\)-algebra where Mathlib's operator concavity of \(\log\) lives.
  Negating concavity of \(\log\) there and pulling back the Loewner inequality gives convexity of
  \(-\log\) on \(\operatorname{Matrix}\).
\end{proof}

n33799.title: Hansen--Pedersen--Jensen operator-Jensen inequality
n33799.content:
\begin{theorem}[Hansen--Pedersen--Jensen operator-Jensen inequality]\label{hpj_affine}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.Lieb.hpj_affine}\leanok
  Let \(f\) be operator convex on an interval \(I\), let \(A,B\) be a contraction pair
  (\(A^{*}A + B^{*}B = 1\)), and let \(X,Y\) be self-adjoint with spectra in \(I\). Then
  \[
    f\bigl(A^{*}XA + B^{*}YB\bigr) \;\le\; A^{*}f(X)A + B^{*}f(Y)B.
  \]
\end{theorem}

n33800.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{operatorConvexOn_neg_log}
  The Effros / Hansen--Pedersen unitary-dilation method. Work in the doubled algebra
  \(\operatorname{Matrix}(\operatorname{Fin}2\times\operatorname{Fin}N)\), form the block diagonal \(D = \mathrm{diag}(X,Y)\), dilate the
  column isometry \([A;B]\) to a unitary \(U\), and pinch \(M = U^{*}DU\) by the involution
  \(V = \mathrm{diag}(1,-1)\): \(\tfrac12 M + \tfrac12 VMV = \mathrm{diag}(M_{00},M_{11})\).
  Operator convexity of \(f\) at dimension \(2N\), applied to \(M\) and \(VMV\), yields
  \(f(\mathrm{diag}(M_{00},M_{11}))\le\mathrm{diag}(f(M)_{00},f(M)_{11})\) blockwise, whose
  \((0,0)\)-block is exactly the asserted inequality. (This node is stated for a general
  operator-convex \(f\) and specialized below to \(f = -\log\).)
\end{proof}

n33801.title: Operator perspective
n33801.content:
\begin{definition}[Operator perspective]\label{operatorPerspective}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.Lieb.operatorPerspective}\leanok
  For \(f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\) and matrices \(L,R\) with \(R\) positive definite, the \emph{operator
  perspective} is
  \[
    P_f(L,R) \;=\; R^{1/2}\,f\bigl(R^{-1/2}\,L\,R^{-1/2}\bigr)\,R^{1/2},
  \]
  with the functional calculus and real powers supplied by the continuous functional calculus.
\end{definition}

n33802.title: Effros' theorem: joint convexity of the perspective

n33803.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{operatorPerspective, hpj_affine}
  The Effros argument, a single application of \Cref{hpj_affine}. Writing \(R = cR_1 + (1-c)R_2\),
  the contraction pair \(A = \sqrt{c}\,R_1^{1/2}R^{-1/2}\), \(B = \sqrt{1-c}\,R_2^{1/2}R^{-1/2}\)
  satisfies \(A^{*}A + B^{*}B = R^{-1/2}RR^{-1/2} = 1\), and the self-adjoint arguments are
  \(X = R_1^{-1/2}L_1R_1^{-1/2}\), \(Y = R_2^{-1/2}L_2R_2^{-1/2}\). Applying
  Hansen--Pedersen--Jensen and conjugating the resulting inequality by \(R^{1/2}\) reproduces
  exactly the joint-convexity estimate, once the sandwich cancellations \(R^{1/2}R^{-1/2} = 1\)
  are used on both sides.
\end{proof}

n33804.title: Operator perspective at a general index

n33805.title: Effros' theorem at a general finite index

n33806.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{opPersp, operatorPerspective_jointly_convex}
  Transport along the star-algebra equivalence
  \(\operatorname{Matrix}(m)\simeq\operatorname{Matrix}(\operatorname{Fin}(\left\lvert m \right\rvert))\) (a reindexing), which preserves positive definiteness,
  self-adjointness, spectra, the continuous functional calculus, real powers, and the Loewner
  order. Push the pair through the equivalence, invoke
  \Cref{operatorPerspective_jointly_convex} on \(\operatorname{Fin}(\left\lvert m \right\rvert)\), and reflect the resulting Loewner
  inequality back.
\end{proof}

n33807.title: Logarithm of a Kronecker product

n33808.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  Simultaneously diagonalize by \(U_A\otimes U_B\); the Kronecker of the two eigenvalue diagonals
  is \(\mathrm{diag}(a_i b_j)\), and \(\log(a_i b_j) = \log a_i + \log b_j\) splits the diagonal
  cfc additively across the two factors. Conjugating back by \(U_A\otimes U_B\) gives the stated
  Kronecker splitting of \(\log\).
\end{proof}

n33809.title: Effros realization of the relative entropy
n33809.content:
\begin{lemma}[Effros realization of the relative entropy]\label{opPersp_neg_log_kron}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.Lieb.opPersp_neg_log_kron}\leanok
  For positive-definite \(\rho,\sigma\), the perspective of \(-\log\) at the commuting pair
  \(L = 1\otimes\sigma^{\top}\), \(R = \rho\otimes 1\) has the closed form
  \[
    P_{-\log}\bigl(1\otimes\sigma^{\top},\,\rho\otimes 1\bigr)
      = \bigl(\rho^{1/2}(\log\rho)\rho^{1/2}\bigr)\otimes 1 - \rho\otimes(\log\sigma)^{\top}.
  \]
\end{lemma}

n33810.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{opPersp, cfc_log_kron}
  The sandwiched argument is \(R^{-1/2}LR^{-1/2} = \rho^{-1}\otimes\sigma^{\top}\). Apply
  \Cref{cfc_log_kron} to
  \(-\log(\rho^{-1}\otimes\sigma^{\top}) = \log\rho\otimes 1 - 1\otimes(\log\sigma)^{\top}\)
  (using \(\log(\rho^{-1}) = -\log\rho\) and the transpose-commutes-with-cfc identity
  \((\log\sigma)^{\top} = \log(\sigma^{\top})\)), then conjugate by
  \(R^{1/2} = \rho^{1/2}\otimes 1\) and cancel with the sandwich to obtain the closed form.
\end{proof}

n33811.title: Scalar Effros functional
n33811.content:
\begin{lemma}[Scalar Effros functional]\label{relForm_opPersp_neg_log}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.Lieb.relForm_opPersp_neg_log}\leanok
  The positive linear functional \(M\mapsto\langle\mathrm{vec}\,1,\,M\,\mathrm{vec}\,1\rangle\)
  recovers the trace-form relative entropy from the perspective:
  \[
    \mathrm{relForm}\,P_{-\log}\bigl(1\otimes\sigma^{\top},\,\rho\otimes 1\bigr)
      = \Tr\bigl(\rho\,(\log\rho - \log\sigma)\bigr).
  \]
\end{lemma}

n33812.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{opPersp_neg_log_kron}
  Apply \(\mathrm{relForm}\) to the closed form of \Cref{opPersp_neg_log_kron}. On Kronecker
  products \(\mathrm{relForm}(A\otimes C) = \Tr(AC^{\top})\), so the two terms become
  \(\Tr(\rho^{1/2}(\log\rho)\rho^{1/2}) = \Tr(\rho\log\rho)\) and \(\Tr(\rho\log\sigma)\); their
  difference is the trace-form relative entropy.
\end{proof}

n33813.title: Trace-form relative entropy

n33814.title: Lieb's theorem: joint convexity of relative entropy
n33814.content:
\begin{theorem}[Lieb's theorem: joint convexity of relative entropy]\label{relEntropyMat_jointly_convex}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.Lieb.relEntropyMat_jointly_convex}\leanok
  For positive-definite \(\rho_1,\rho_2,\sigma_1,\sigma_2\) and \(c\in[0,1]\),
  \[
    \mathrm{relEntropyMat}\bigl(c\rho_1 + (1-c)\rho_2,\;c\sigma_1 + (1-c)\sigma_2\bigr)
      \le c\,\mathrm{relEntropyMat}(\rho_1,\sigma_1) + (1-c)\,\mathrm{relEntropyMat}(\rho_2,\sigma_2).
  \]
\end{theorem}

n33815.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{relEntropyMat, opPersp_jointly_convex, operatorConvexOn_neg_log, relForm_opPersp_neg_log}
  Lieb's theorem (Lieb 1973; Carlen, \emph{Trace Inequalities and Quantum Entropy}, Thm.~2.12), obtained from
  Effros' joint convexity of the perspective. The maps \(\rho\mapsto R = \rho\otimes 1\) and
  \(\sigma\mapsto L = 1\otimes\sigma^{\top}\) are \(\mathbb{R}\)-linear, so applying
  \Cref{opPersp_jointly_convex} to \(f = -\log\) (operator convex on \((0,\infty)\) by
  \Cref{operatorConvexOn_neg_log}) gives a Loewner joint-convexity inequality for the perspective.
  The functional \(\mathrm{relForm}\) is positive and linear; by \Cref{relForm_opPersp_neg_log} it
  turns that operator inequality into the scalar convexity of
  \((\rho,\sigma)\mapsto\Tr(\rho(\log\rho - \log\sigma))\), whose real part is
  \(\mathrm{relEntropyMat}\).
\end{proof}

n33816.title: Finite Jensen form of Lieb's theorem
n33816.content:
\begin{lemma}[Finite Jensen form of Lieb's theorem]\label{relEntropyMat_convex_sum}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.Lieb.relEntropyMat_convex_sum}\leanok
  For a finite convex combination of faithful states --- weights \(w_i\ge 0\) with
  \(\sum_i w_i = 1\) and positive-definite \(\rho_i,\sigma_i\) ---,
  \[
    \mathrm{relEntropyMat}\Bigl(\sum_i w_i\rho_i,\;\sum_i w_i\sigma_i\Bigr)
      \;\le\; \sum_i w_i\,\mathrm{relEntropyMat}(\rho_i,\sigma_i).
  \]
\end{lemma}

n33817.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{relEntropyMat_jointly_convex}
  The two-point joint convexity of \Cref{relEntropyMat_jointly_convex} says
  \(\mathrm{relEntropyMat}\) is a convex function on the set of pairs of positive-definite
  matrices; Jensen's inequality for a convex function over a finite convex combination upgrades
  the two-point estimate to the finite-sum form.
\end{proof}

n33818.title: Bridge to the spectral relative entropy

n33819.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{relEntropyMat, relEntropy_eq_traceLog}
  Both sides expand through the spectral theorem: the trace form
  \(\Re\,\Tr(\rho(\log\rho - \log\sigma))\) equals the spectral double sum defining
  \(S(\rho\|\sigma)\) once the Hermitian cfc is written via eigendecompositions
  (this is \Cref{relEntropy_eq_traceLog} together with the eigenbasis form of the functional
  calculus). Hence the trace-form joint convexity above transfers to the Umegaki relative entropy
  on density matrices.
\end{proof}

n33820.title: The partial-trace DPI, as a monomorphic \texttt{Prop}
n33820.content:
\begin{definition}[The partial-trace DPI, as a monomorphic \texttt{Prop}]\label{RelEntropyMonotoneUnderPartialTrace}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.RelEntropyMonotoneUnderPartialTrace}\leanok
  \uses{relEntropy, partialTraceRight}
  \texttt{RelEntropyMonotoneUnderPartialTrace} is the proposition that for all finite index types
  \(n_A, n_E\) and all states \(\rho,\sigma\) on \(n_A\times n_E\) with \(\sigma\) faithful
  (positive definite), tracing out the \(E\)-factor does not increase relative entropy,
  \[
    S\bigl(\Tr_E\rho\,\big\|\,\Tr_E\sigma\bigr) \;\le\; S(\rho\|\sigma).
  \]
  The index types are quantified over \texttt{Type} (universe \(0\)): finite-dimensional quantum
  information lives in universe \(0\), and pinning the universe lets this \texttt{Prop} be used as
  a reusable hypothesis whose subsystems unify with any consumer's.
\end{definition}

n33821.title: Partial-trace DPI, faithful case
n33821.content:
\begin{theorem}[Partial-trace DPI, faithful case]\label{relEntropyMonotone_partialTrace_faithful}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.Lieb.relEntropyMonotone_partialTrace_faithful}\leanok
  For positive-definite states \(\rho,\sigma\) on \(n_A\times n_E\),
  \[
    S\bigl(\Tr_E\rho\,\big\|\,\Tr_E\sigma\bigr) \;\le\; S(\rho\|\sigma).
  \]
\end{theorem}

n33822.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{relEntropyMat_convex_sum, relEntropy_conj_invariant, relEntropy_ancilla_invariant}
  Realize the partial trace as a Weyl twirl: with \(d = \#n_E\) and \(\tau = \tfrac1d\mathbf 1\)
  the maximally mixed ancilla state, averaging \(\rho\) over the \(d^2\) Heisenberg--Weyl unitaries
  \(W_{ab}\) on the \(E\)-factor gives
  \(d^{-2}\sum_{a,b}(\mathbf 1\otimes W_{ab})\rho(\mathbf 1\otimes W_{ab})^{*}
  = (\Tr_E\rho)\otimes\tau\), and likewise for \(\sigma\). Each twirled state
  \(\rho_{ab} := (\mathbf 1\otimes W_{ab})\rho(\mathbf 1\otimes W_{ab})^{*}\) has
  \(S(\rho_{ab}\|\sigma_{ab}) = S(\rho\|\sigma)\) by unitary invariance
  (\Cref{relEntropy_conj_invariant}), and the averaged pair has relative entropy
  \(S\bigl((\Tr_E\rho)\otimes\tau\,\|\,(\Tr_E\sigma)\otimes\tau\bigr) = S(\Tr_E\rho\|\Tr_E\sigma)\)
  by ancilla additivity (\Cref{relEntropy_ancilla_invariant}). The finite-sum form of Lieb's joint
  convexity (\Cref{relEntropyMat_convex_sum}) applied to the weights \(w_{ab} = d^{-2}\) then
  yields \(S(\Tr_E\rho\|\Tr_E\sigma)\le\sum_{ab} w_{ab}\,S(\rho_{ab}\|\sigma_{ab}) = S(\rho\|\sigma)\).
\end{proof}

n33823.title: Partial-trace DPI, unconditional

n33824.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{RelEntropyMonotoneUnderPartialTrace, relEntropyMonotone_partialTrace_faithful}
  Regularize the first argument along the affine path
  \(\rho_\varepsilon = (1-\varepsilon)\rho + \varepsilon\tau\) towards the maximally mixed state
  \(\tau\). For \(\varepsilon\in(0,1]\) the state \(\rho_\varepsilon\) is positive definite, so the
  faithful case (\Cref{relEntropyMonotone_partialTrace_faithful}) gives
  \(S(\Tr_E\rho_\varepsilon\|\Tr_E\sigma)\le S(\rho_\varepsilon\|\sigma)\). Both sides are
  continuous in \(\varepsilon\) at \(0\) (continuity of \(M\mapsto S(M\|\sigma)\) on states with
  \(\sigma\) fixed and faithful, and continuity of the partial trace), and
  \(\rho_\varepsilon\to\rho\); passing to the limit \(\varepsilon\downarrow 0\) preserves the
  inequality.
\end{proof}

n33825.title: Tracing out an adjoined ancilla is the identity

n33827.title: Isometric-embedding invariance
n33827.content:
\begin{theorem}[Isometric-embedding invariance]\label{relEntropy_embed_invariant}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.relEntropy_embed_invariant}\leanok
  For states \(\rho,\sigma\) on \(n\), a faithful ancilla \(\alpha\) on \(e\), a unitary \(U\) on
  \(n\times e\), and faithful \(\sigma\),
  \[
    S\bigl(U(\rho\otimes\alpha)U^{*}\,\big\|\,U(\sigma\otimes\alpha)U^{*}\bigr) \;=\; S(\rho\|\sigma).
  \]
\end{theorem}

n33829.title: Stinespring reduction of the DPI
n33829.content:
\begin{theorem}[Stinespring reduction of the DPI]\label{stinespring_relEntropy_monotone}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.stinespring_relEntropy_monotone}\leanok
  \emph{Given} the partial-trace DPI (\Cref{RelEntropyMonotoneUnderPartialTrace}), every
  Stinespring-dilated channel \(\Lambda\rho = \Tr_E\bigl(U(\rho\otimes\alpha)U^{*}\bigr)\) ---
  adjoin a faithful ancilla \(\alpha\), conjugate by a unitary dilation \(U\), then trace out the
  ancilla --- is relative-entropy monotone on faithful states:
  \(S(\Lambda\rho\|\Lambda\sigma)\le S(\rho\|\sigma)\).
\end{theorem}

n33830.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{RelEntropyMonotoneUnderPartialTrace, relEntropy_embed_invariant}
  Apply the wall (\Cref{RelEntropyMonotoneUnderPartialTrace}) to the dilated states
  \(U(\rho\otimes\alpha)U^{*}\) and \(U(\sigma\otimes\alpha)U^{*}\) (the latter faithful, being a
  unitary conjugate of a Kronecker product of faithful states): tracing out the ancilla gives
  \(S(\Tr_E U(\rho\otimes\alpha)U^{*}\|\Tr_E U(\sigma\otimes\alpha)U^{*})\le
  S(U(\rho\otimes\alpha)U^{*}\|U(\sigma\otimes\alpha)U^{*})\). The right-hand side equals
  \(S(\rho\|\sigma)\) by isometric-embedding invariance (\Cref{relEntropy_embed_invariant}).
\end{proof}

n33831.title: Data-processing inequality for the faithful-ancilla mixed-Stinespring family
n33831.content:
\begin{theorem}[Data-processing inequality for the faithful-ancilla mixed-Stinespring family]\label{monotonicity_relEntropy_under_stinespring}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.monotonicity_relEntropy_under_stinespring}\leanok
  Unconditionally, for a faithful ancilla \(\alpha\), a unitary dilation \(U\), and faithful
  \(\sigma\),
  \[
    S\bigl(\Tr_E U(\rho\otimes\alpha)U^{*}\,\big\|\,\Tr_E U(\sigma\otimes\alpha)U^{*}\bigr)
      \;\le\; S(\rho\|\sigma).
  \]
  This is the data-processing inequality for the faithful-ancilla mixed-Stinespring family; that
  family does \emph{not} contain every CPTP channel (amplitude damping lies outside it, since its
  exact dilation needs a pure, non-faithful ancilla), so it is not an in-repo DPI for a general
  Kraus channel.
\end{theorem}

n33833.title: No faithful-monotone recovery section under a strict drop
n33833.content:
\begin{theorem}[No faithful-monotone recovery section under a strict drop]\label{no_section_of_strict_relEntropy_drop}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.no_section_of_strict_relEntropy_drop}\leanok
  If a map \(R\) satisfies the faithful data-processing inequality and inverts a coarse-graining
  \(\Lambda\) on the pair \(\rho,\sigma\) (\(R(\Lambda\rho) = \rho\), \(R(\Lambda\sigma) = \sigma\)
  with \(\Lambda\sigma\) faithful), then a \emph{strict} drop
  \(S(\Lambda\rho\|\Lambda\sigma) < S(\rho\|\sigma)\) is impossible.
\end{theorem}

n33834.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  Monotonicity of \(R\) applied to \(\Lambda\rho,\Lambda\sigma\) gives
  \(S(R(\Lambda\rho)\|R(\Lambda\sigma))\le S(\Lambda\rho\|\Lambda\sigma)\); the section identities
  rewrite the left side as \(S(\rho\|\sigma)\), so
  \(S(\rho\|\sigma)\le S(\Lambda\rho\|\Lambda\sigma)\), contradicting the assumed strict drop.
\end{proof}

n33835.title: No Stinespring recovery under a strict drop

n33837.title: Kraus channel
n33837.content:
\begin{definition}[Kraus channel]\label{KrausChannel}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.KrausChannel}\leanok
  A \emph{Kraus channel} on \(\operatorname{Matrix}_n(\mathbb{C})\) is a finite family of Kraus operators
  \(K : \iota\to\operatorname{Matrix}_n(\mathbb{C})\) satisfying the completeness relation
  \(\sum_i K_i^{\dagger}K_i = 1\). Its \emph{Schr\"odinger action} is
  \(\Lambda(X)=\sum_i K_i\,X\,K_i^{\dagger}\) (Lean: \texttt{toMat}, restricted to states as
  \texttt{toDM}), and its \emph{Heisenberg (Hilbert--Schmidt) adjoint} is
  \(\Lambda^{\dagger}(X)=\sum_i K_i^{\dagger}X\,K_i\) (Lean: \texttt{adj}).
\end{definition}

n33838.title: Trace preservation

n33840.title: Petz recovery map

n33841.title: Petz recovery identity
n33841.content:
\begin{theorem}[Petz recovery identity]\label{petz_recovery}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.petz_recovery}\leanok
  If the channel output \(\Lambda\sigma\) is positive definite, then the Petz map recovers
  \(\sigma\) from \(\Lambda\sigma\):
  \[
    P_{\sigma,\Lambda}(\Lambda\sigma) \;=\; \sigma.
  \]
\end{theorem}

n33842.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{petz, KrausChannel.toMat_trace}
  Feeding \(X=\Lambda\sigma\) into \(P_{\sigma,\Lambda}\), the inner conjugation
  \((\Lambda\sigma)^{-1/2}(\Lambda\sigma)(\Lambda\sigma)^{-1/2}=1\) collapses to the identity (this
  is where positive definiteness of \(\Lambda\sigma\) is used); unitality \(\Lambda^{\dagger}(1)=1\)
  then leaves \(\sqrt{\sigma}\cdot 1\cdot\sqrt{\sigma}=\sigma\).
\end{proof}

n33843.title: Recovery \(\Rightarrow\) saturation
n33843.content:
\begin{theorem}[Recovery \(\Rightarrow\) saturation]\label{petz_recovery_implies_equality}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.petz_recovery_implies_equality}\leanok
  Let \(\Lambda\) and \(R\) be maps on states, each monotone under relative entropy (each satisfies
  the data-processing inequality against positive-definite second arguments). If \(R\) is a recovery
  section for the pair \(\rho,\sigma\), i.e.\ \(R(\Lambda\rho)=\rho\) and \(R(\Lambda\sigma)=\sigma\)
  (with \(\sigma,\Lambda\sigma\) positive definite), then the data-processing inequality is
  saturated:
  \[
    S(\Lambda\rho\|\Lambda\sigma) \;=\; S(\rho\|\sigma).
  \]
\end{theorem}

n33844.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  Monotonicity of \(\Lambda\) gives \(S(\Lambda\rho\|\Lambda\sigma)\le S(\rho\|\sigma)\). For the
  reverse inequality, apply monotonicity of \(R\) to the pair \(\Lambda\rho,\Lambda\sigma\) and
  rewrite through the section identities \(R(\Lambda\rho)=\rho\), \(R(\Lambda\sigma)=\sigma\); this
  yields \(S(\rho\|\sigma)\le S(\Lambda\rho\|\Lambda\sigma)\). Antisymmetry gives equality.
\end{proof}

n33845.title: Rectangular isometry \(-\log\) Loewner inequality
n33845.content:
\begin{theorem}[Rectangular isometry \(-\log\) Loewner inequality]\label{rect_isometry_neg_log_loewner}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.Lieb.rect_isometry_neg_log_loewner}\leanok
  Let \(W:\mathbb{C}^q\to\mathbb{C}^p\) be an isometry (\(W^{\dagger}W=1\)) and \(X\) self-adjoint
  with spectrum in \((0,\infty)\). Then
  \[
    (-\log)\bigl(W^{\dagger}X\,W\bigr) \;\le\; W^{\dagger}\,(-\log)(X)\,W .
  \]
\end{theorem}

n33846.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  Extend the orthonormal columns of \(W\) to a unitary \(U\); conjugating \(X\) by \(U\) and
  reindexing, \(W^{\dagger}XW\) is the upper-left corner of \(A=U^{\dagger}XU\). Operator convexity of
  \(-\log\) gives the corner inequality
  \((-\log)(\text{corner of }A)\le\text{corner of }(-\log)(A)\) (\texttt{sum\_corner\_loewner}
  applied to \texttt{operatorConvexOn\_neg\_log}), which is exactly the claim after identifying both
  corners.
\end{proof}

n33847.title: Choi \(-\log\) operator inequality
n33847.content:
\begin{theorem}[Choi \(-\log\) operator inequality]\label{choi-neg-log-loewner-math}
  For Kraus operators \(K\) with \(\sum_i K_i^{\dagger}K_i=1\) and \(X\) self-adjoint with spectrum
  in \((0,\infty)\),
  \[
    (-\log)\!\Bigl(\textstyle\sum_i K_i^{\dagger}X K_i\Bigr)
      \;\le\; \sum_i K_i^{\dagger}\,(-\log)(X)\,K_i .
  \]
\end{theorem}

n33849.title: Modular form of the relative entropy
n33849.content:
\begin{lemma}[Modular form of the relative entropy]\label{kronForm_re_eq_relEntropy}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.Lieb.kronForm_re_eq_relEntropy}\leanok
  For faithful states \(\rho,\sigma\), with (vectorised) relative modular operator
  \(\Delta=\sigma\otimes(\rho^{-1})^{\top}\) and cyclic vector
  \(\xi=\operatorname{vec}(\rho^{1/2})\),
  \[
    S(\rho\|\sigma) \;=\; \operatorname{Re}\bigl\langle\xi,\ (-\log)(\Delta)\,\xi\bigr\rangle .
  \]
\end{lemma}

n33850.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  Compute \((-\log)(\sigma\otimes(\rho^{-1})^{\top})=-(\log\sigma)\otimes 1+1\otimes(\log\rho)^{\top}\)
  (via \(\log\) of a Kronecker product, \(\log\rho^{-1}=-\log\rho\), and the transpose law). Apply
  this to \(\operatorname{vec}(\rho^{1/2})\) through the vec/Kronecker rule
  \((A\otimes B^{\top})\operatorname{vec}X=\operatorname{vec}(AXB)\), read off via the
  Hilbert--Schmidt inner product \(\langle\operatorname{vec}X,\operatorname{vec}Y\rangle=\tr(X^{\dagger}Y)\),
  and use \(\rho^{1/2}\rho^{1/2}=\rho\) with trace cyclicity to obtain
  \(\tr(\rho(\log\rho-\log\sigma))=S(\rho\|\sigma)\).
\end{proof}

n33851.title: Scalar channel \(-\log\) modular gap
n33851.content:
\begin{theorem}[Scalar channel \(-\log\) modular gap]\label{channel_modular_gap}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.Lieb.channel_modular_gap}\leanok
  For a Kraus channel \(\Lambda\) with all four states \(\rho,\sigma,\Lambda\rho,\Lambda\sigma\)
  faithful, if data processing is saturated (\(S(\rho\|\sigma)=S(\Lambda\rho\|\Lambda\sigma)\)), then
  the two \(-\log\) modular quadratic forms agree at the output cyclic vector
  \(\xi=\operatorname{vec}((\Lambda\rho)^{1/2})\):
  \[
    \operatorname{Re}\bigl\langle\xi,\ W^{\dagger}(-\log\Delta)W\,\xi\bigr\rangle
      \;=\; \operatorname{Re}\bigl\langle\xi,\ (-\log\Delta_{\mathrm{out}})\,\xi\bigr\rangle,
  \]
  with \(W=\texttt{petzWChanVec}\), \(\Delta=\sigma\otimes(\rho^{-1})^{\top}\),
  \(\Delta_{\mathrm{out}}=(\Lambda\sigma)\otimes((\Lambda\rho)^{-1})^{\top}\).
\end{theorem}

n33853.title: Injectivity-free gap decomposition
n33853.content:
\begin{lemma}[Injectivity-free gap decomposition]\label{contraction_gap_decomp}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.Lieb.contraction_gap_decomp}\leanok
  For a contraction \(W\) with defect \((1-W^{\dagger}W)\xi=0\), positive-definite shifts
  \(X,\mathrm{Out}\), writing \(\eta=\mathrm{Out}^{-1}\xi\), \(b=X^{-1}(W\xi)-W\eta\),
  \(Y=W^{\dagger}XW\),
  \[
    \bigl\langle\xi,\ (W^{\dagger}X^{-1}W-\mathrm{Out}^{-1})\,\xi\bigr\rangle
      \;=\; \langle b,\ X\,b\rangle \;+\; \langle\eta,\ (\mathrm{Out}-Y)\,\eta\rangle .
  \]
\end{lemma}

n33854.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  A pure matrix identity: the isometric proof's \(Y^{-1}\) bridge is replaced by
  \(\mathrm{Out}^{-1}Y\mathrm{Out}^{-1}\), which cancels between the two summands, so the compression
  \(Y\) is never inverted. Expanding \(\langle b,Xb\rangle\) produces \(W^{\dagger}X^{-1}W\), two
  cross terms \(W^{\dagger}W\mathrm{Out}^{-1}\) and \(\mathrm{Out}^{-1}(W^{\dagger}W)\), and
  \(\mathrm{Out}^{-1}Y\mathrm{Out}^{-1}\); the contraction defect collapses each cross term (each
  contains \(W^{\dagger}W\xi=\xi\)) to \(\mathrm{Out}^{-1}\), and the second summand contributes
  \(\mathrm{Out}^{-1}-\mathrm{Out}^{-1}Y\mathrm{Out}^{-1}\). Adding and simplifying leaves exactly
  \(W^{\dagger}X^{-1}W-\mathrm{Out}^{-1}\).
\end{proof}

n33855.title: Per-\(t\) intertwining at gap zero
n33855.content:
\begin{lemma}[Per-\(t\) intertwining at gap zero]\label{contraction_perT_intertwine_of_gap_zero}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.Lieb.contraction_perT_intertwine_of_gap_zero}\leanok
  In the setting of Lemma~\ref{contraction_gap_decomp}, with the compression bound
  \(W^{\dagger}XW\le\mathrm{Out}\), if the total resolvent gap
  \(\operatorname{Re}\langle\xi,(W^{\dagger}X^{-1}W-\mathrm{Out}^{-1})\xi\rangle\) vanishes, then
  \(X^{-1}(W\xi)=W(\mathrm{Out}^{-1}\xi)\).
\end{lemma}

n33856.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{contraction_gap_decomp}
  Both summands of Lemma~\ref{contraction_gap_decomp} are nonnegative (\(X\succ 0\) and
  \(\mathrm{Out}-Y\succeq 0\)), and their real parts sum to the vanishing gap; hence each is zero. In
  particular \(\operatorname{Re}\langle b,Xb\rangle=0\), and positive definiteness of \(X\) forces
  \(b=0\), i.e.\ \(X^{-1}(W\xi)=W(\mathrm{Out}^{-1}\xi)\).
\end{proof}

n33857.title: Scalar-sourced contraction rigidity spine
n33857.content:
\begin{theorem}[Scalar-sourced contraction rigidity spine]\label{contraction_resolvent_intertwine_of_re_eq}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.Lieb.contraction_resolvent_intertwine_of_re_eq}\leanok
  Let \(W\) be a contraction (\(W^{\dagger}W\le 1\)), \(\Delta,\Delta_{\mathrm{out}}\) positive
  definite with compression bound \(W^{\dagger}\Delta W\le\Delta_{\mathrm{out}}\), cyclic-norm
  condition \(\left\lVert W\xi \right\rVert=\left\lVert \xi \right\rVert\), and the \emph{scalar} \(-\log\) saturation
  \(\operatorname{Re}\langle\xi,W^{\dagger}(-\log\Delta)W\xi\rangle
    =\operatorname{Re}\langle\xi,(-\log\Delta_{\mathrm{out}})\xi\rangle\).
  Then for every \(t>0\),
  \[
    (\Delta+t)^{-1}(W\xi) \;=\; W\bigl((\Delta_{\mathrm{out}}+t)^{-1}\xi\bigr).
  \]
\end{theorem}

n33858.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{contraction_perT_intertwine_of_gap_zero}
  Represent \(-\log\) by the integral \(\int_0^\infty\bigl((1+t)^{-1}-(\cdot+t)^{-1}\bigr)\,dt\) and
  let \(F(t)\) be the real resolvent-gap quadratic form at \(\xi\). By the shifted compression bound
  \(W^{\dagger}(\Delta+t)W\le\Delta_{\mathrm{out}}+t\) and the injectivity-free decomposition,
  \(F(t)\ge 0\) pointwise; integrating recovers the scalar \(-\log\) gap, which is \(0\) by
  hypothesis. A nonnegative continuous integrand with zero integral vanishes on \((0,\infty)\), so
  each \(F(t)=0\); per-\(t\) saturation (Lemma~\ref{contraction_perT_intertwine_of_gap_zero}) gives
  the resolvent intertwining. (The general finite square index follows by an \texttt{equivFin}
  reindexing.)
\end{proof}

n33859.title: Contraction intertwines every continuous function
n33859.content:
\begin{lemma}[Contraction intertwines every continuous function]\label{contraction_cfc_intertwine}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.Lieb.contraction_cfc_intertwine}\leanok
  Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{contraction_resolvent_intertwine_of_re_eq}, for every
  continuous \(g\),
  \[
    W\bigl(g(\Delta_{\mathrm{out}})\,\xi\bigr) \;=\; g(\Delta)\,(W\xi).
  \]
\end{lemma}

n33860.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{contraction_resolvent_intertwine_of_re_eq}
  On the finite union of the two spectra, \(g\) is a real-coefficient combination of resolvents
  \(x\mapsto(x+t)^{-1}\) (finite-spectrum resolvent readoff). Both \(g(\Delta_{\mathrm{out}})\) and
  \(g(\Delta)\) become the corresponding operator-resolvent combinations, and the per-resolvent
  intertwining of Theorem~\ref{contraction_resolvent_intertwine_of_re_eq} propagates linearly.
\end{proof}

n33861.title: Channel unitary-power intertwining

n33863.title: Modular \(it\)-intertwining
n33863.content:
\begin{definition}[Modular \(it\)-intertwining]\label{IntertwinesIt}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.Lieb.IntertwinesIt}\leanok
  The channel adjoint \emph{intertwines the modular \(it\)-flows} if, for all \(t\),
  \[
    \Lambda^{\dagger}\bigl((\Lambda\rho)^{it}(\Lambda\sigma)^{-it}\bigr) \;=\; \rho^{it}\,\sigma^{-it}.
  \]
\end{definition}

n33864.title: Equality \(\Rightarrow\) modular intertwining (general channel)

n33865.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{channel_upow_intertwine, IntertwinesIt}
  From Theorem~\ref{channel_upow_intertwine}, reading off the vec-action
  \(\Delta^{it}\operatorname{vec}X=\operatorname{vec}(P^{it}XR^{-it})\) turns the vectorised statement
  into \(\Lambda^{\dagger}\)-form directly (the vectorised Petz map already contains
  \(\Lambda^{\dagger}\), so no amplification is needed). Cancelling the \((\Lambda\rho)^{\pm 1/2}\)
  twist on the input column and the \(\rho^{1/2}\) factor, then taking adjoints, yields
  \(\Lambda^{\dagger}((\Lambda\rho)^{it}(\Lambda\sigma)^{-it})=\rho^{it}\sigma^{-it}\).
\end{proof}

n33866.title: Modular intertwining \(\Rightarrow\) Petz recovery

n33867.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{IntertwinesIt, petz}
  Analytic continuation of the \(it\)-intertwining to the value \(t=-i/2\) (a Kadison-type argument on
  the modular flow) turns the cocycle identity into
  \(\sqrt{\sigma}\,\Lambda^{\dagger}((\Lambda\sigma)^{-1/2}(\Lambda\rho)(\Lambda\sigma)^{-1/2})\sqrt{\sigma}=\rho\),
  which is exactly \(P_{\sigma,\Lambda}(\Lambda\rho)=\rho\).
\end{proof}

n33868.title: General Petz recovery from equality --- issue \#28 headline
n33868.content:
\begin{theorem}[General Petz recovery from equality --- issue \#28 headline]\label{petz_equality_recovery_general}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.Lieb.petz_equality_recovery_general}\leanok
  Let \(\Lambda\) be \emph{any} Kraus channel and \(\rho,\sigma\) states with all four of
  \(\rho,\sigma,\Lambda\rho,\Lambda\sigma\) positive definite. If data processing is saturated,
  \[
    S(\rho\|\sigma) \;=\; S(\Lambda\rho\|\Lambda\sigma),
  \]
  then the Petz recovery map reconstructs the input state,
  \[
    P_{\sigma,\Lambda}(\Lambda\rho) \;=\; \rho .
  \]
  No injectivity of the channel (or of the vectorised Petz map) is assumed; the result holds for
  information-losing channels such as the completely depolarising channel.
\end{theorem}

n33869.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{channel_equality_imp_intertwinesIt, intertwinesIt_imp_recovery}
  Compose Theorem~\ref{channel_equality_imp_intertwinesIt} (entropy equality \(\Rightarrow\) modular
  \(it\)-intertwining) with Theorem~\ref{intertwinesIt_imp_recovery} (intertwining \(\Rightarrow\)
  recovery). This is the full-generality form of Petz (2003, Thm~2). Together with
  Theorem~\ref{petz_recovery_implies_equality} it closes the equivalence: for faithful states,
  saturation of the data-processing inequality holds if and only if the Petz map recovers the input.
\end{proof}

n33870.title: Partial-trace modular gap
n33870.content:
\begin{theorem}[Partial-trace modular gap]\label{partialTrace_modular_gap}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.Lieb.partialTrace_modular_gap}\leanok
  If the partial-trace relative entropy is preserved,
  \(S(\operatorname{Tr}_B\omega\|\operatorname{Tr}_B\tau)=S(\omega\|\tau)\), then the rectangular
  \(-\log\) operator-Jensen gap for the Petz isometry \(W\) annihilates the output cyclic vector
  \(\xi=\operatorname{vec}((\operatorname{Tr}_B\omega)^{1/2})\):
  \[
    \bigl(W^{\dagger}(-\log)(\Delta)\,W\bigr)\,\xi
      \;=\; (-\log)\bigl(W^{\dagger}\Delta\,W\bigr)\,\xi,
    \qquad \Delta=\tau\otimes(\omega^{-1})^{\top}.
  \]
\end{theorem}

n33871.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{rect_isometry_neg_log_loewner, kronForm_re_eq_relEntropy}
  By Theorem~\ref{rect_isometry_neg_log_loewner} the operator \(B-A\ge 0\), where
  \(B=W^{\dagger}(-\log)(\Delta)W\) and \(A=(-\log)(W^{\dagger}\Delta W)\). Using
  Lemma~\ref{kronForm_re_eq_relEntropy} on both sides (the compression \(W^{\dagger}\Delta W\) is
  exactly the output modular operator, and \(W\xi=\operatorname{vec}(\omega^{1/2})\)), the two
  quadratic forms at \(\xi\) equal \(S(\operatorname{Tr}_B\omega\|\operatorname{Tr}_B\tau)\) and
  \(S(\omega\|\tau)\); the entropy equality makes
  \(\operatorname{Re}\langle\xi,(B-A)\xi\rangle=0\). For a positive semidefinite matrix a vanishing
  real expectation forces \((B-A)\xi=0\).
\end{proof}

n33872.title: Partial-trace equality \(\Rightarrow\) modular intertwining
n33872.content:
\begin{theorem}[Partial-trace equality \(\Rightarrow\) modular intertwining]\label{partialTrace_equality_imp_intertwinesIt}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.Lieb.partialTrace_equality_imp_intertwinesIt}\leanok
  Under the same entropy-preservation hypothesis, the amplified output modular \(it\)-cocycle equals
  the input one, for all \(t\in\mathbb{R}\):
  \[
    \bigl((\operatorname{Tr}_B\omega)^{it}(\operatorname{Tr}_B\tau)^{-it}\bigr)\otimes 1
      \;=\; \omega^{it}\,\tau^{-it}.
  \]
\end{theorem}

n33873.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{partialTrace_modular_gap, IntertwinesIt}
  The gap of Theorem~\ref{partialTrace_modular_gap} is upgraded, first to an intertwining of every
  resolvent \((\Delta+t)^{-1}\) (the isometric rigidity tail), then --- via a finite-spectrum
  resolvent readoff --- to the intertwining of \emph{every} continuous function of \(\Delta\) on
  \(\xi\). Feeding the pair \(\cos(t\log\cdot),\sin(t\log\cdot)\) assembles the unitary power
  \(\Delta^{it}\), giving \(W(\Delta_A^{it}\xi)=\Delta^{it}(W\xi)\). Reading off the vec-action
  \(\Delta^{it}\operatorname{vec}X=\operatorname{vec}(P^{it}XR^{-it})\), cancelling the
  \(\omega_A^{\pm 1/2}\) twist on the input column and the \(\omega^{1/2}\) factor, and taking adjoints
  yields the stated cocycle identity --- an instance of the general \texttt{IntertwinesIt} property
  (Definition~\ref{IntertwinesIt}).
\end{proof}

n33874.title: Unital \(*\)-endomorphism
n33874.content:
\begin{definition}[Unital \(*\)-endomorphism]\label{UnitalStarEndo}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.CNT.UnitalStarEndo}\leanok
  A \emph{finite quantum dynamics} is a map \(\Phi:\operatorname{Matrix}_d(\mathbb{C})\to\operatorname{Matrix}_d(\mathbb{C})\)
  that is additive, multiplicative, unital (\(\Phi(1)=1\)) and \(*\)-preserving
  (\(\Phi(x^{\dagger})=\Phi(x)^{\dagger}\)). Additivity is carried as part of the datum: it is
  automatic for a \(*\)-homomorphism of matrix algebras, and it is exactly what lets \(\Phi\) commute
  with the finite sums appearing in the telescoping identity below.
\end{definition}

n33875.title: Operational partition of unity

n33876.title: Time-ordered refinement
n33876.content:
\begin{definition}[Time-ordered refinement]\label{refine}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.CNT.refine}\leanok
  \uses{UnitalStarEndo, OperationalPartition}
  Given a dynamics \(\Phi\) and an operational partition \(X=(x_i)\), the \emph{time-ordered
  refinement} of depth \(n\) along a word \(f\in(\operatorname{Fin}k)^{\operatorname{Fin}n}\) is the operator
  \[
    \mathrm{refine}\,\Phi\,X\,n\,f \;=\;
      x_{f_0}\,\Phi(x_{f_1})\,\Phi^{2}(x_{f_2})\cdots\Phi^{n-1}(x_{f_{n-1}}),
  \]
  defined by the telescoping recursion
  \(\mathrm{refine}(n+1,f)=x_{f_0}\cdot\Phi\!\bigl(\mathrm{refine}(n,\mathrm{tail}\,f)\bigr)\) with
  \(\mathrm{refine}(0,\cdot)=1\). It records the observable measured along the first \(n\) steps of
  the orbit under \(\Phi\).
\end{definition}

n33877.title: Telescoping identity

n33878.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{refine, OperationalPartition, UnitalStarEndo}
  Induct on \(n\). Splitting the word as \(f=(i,g)\) with \(i=f_0\), the summand factors as
  \(\Phi(\mathrm{refine}(n,g))^{\dagger}\,(x_i^{\dagger}x_i)\,\Phi(\mathrm{refine}(n,g))\); summing over
  the leading letter \(i\) and applying \(\sum_i x_i^{\dagger}x_i=1\) removes it. What remains is
  \(\sum_g\Phi\!\bigl(\mathrm{refine}(n,g)^{\dagger}\mathrm{refine}(n,g)\bigr)\); pulling \(\Phi\) out of
  the finite sum (its additivity, Definition~\ref{UnitalStarEndo}) and applying the inductive
  hypothesis leaves \(\Phi(1)=1\).
\end{proof}

n33879.title: Correlation density matrix

n33880.title: CNT/ALF dynamical entropy
n33880.content:
\begin{definition}[CNT/ALF dynamical entropy]\label{cntDynamicalEntropy}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.CNT.cntDynamicalEntropy}\leanok
  \uses{corrMatrix}
  The \emph{entropy of a partition} is the infimum von Neumann entropy rate
  \[
    h_\Phi(\rho,X)\;=\;\inf_{n\ge 1}\ \frac{S\!\bigl(\mathrm{corrMatrix}\,\Phi\,\rho\,X\,n\bigr)}{n},
    \qquad S(\tau)=-\tr(\tau\log\tau),
  \]
  and the \emph{CNT dynamical entropy} of \(\Phi\) in the state \(\rho\) is the supremum over all
  finite operational partitions, \(h_\Phi(\rho)=\sup_{k,X}h_\Phi(\rho,X)\) (valued in
  \(\overline{\mathbb{R}}\)). The \(\inf_n\) form is the honest analogue of the subadditive limit
  \(\lim_n S(\cdot)/n\) and sidesteps an operator-Fekete argument.
\end{definition}

n33881.title: Diagonal state

n33882.title: Projection partition

n33883.title: The permutation dynamics (abelian corner)

n33884.title: Per-resolution diagonal collapse
n33884.content:
\begin{theorem}[Per-resolution diagonal collapse]\label{vonNeumannEntropy_corrMatrix_eq_ksEntropySeq}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.CNT.vonNeumannEntropy_corrMatrix_eq_ksEntropySeq}\leanok
  On the abelian corner the correlation matrix is diagonal, carrying the masses of the classical
  \(n\)-fold join on its diagonal; hence its von Neumann entropy equals the classical iterated-join
  Shannon entropy of the system \((\operatorname{Fin}d,\mu,\sigma)\):
  \[
    S\!\bigl(\mathrm{corrMatrix}\,(\mathrm{adPerm}\,\sigma)\,\rho_\mu\,(\mathrm{projPartition}\,c)\,n\bigr)
      \;=\; H\!\Bigl(\textstyle\bigvee_{l<n}\sigma^{-l}\,c^{-1}(\cdot)\Bigr).
  \]
\end{theorem}

n33885.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{corrMatrix, adPerm, refine, projPartition, densityOfPMF}
  Because \(\mathrm{adPerm}\,\sigma\) preserves diagonal matrices, the refinement of a projection
  partition is again diagonal, and the depth-\(n\) refinement product along a word \(f\) is exactly
  the indicator of the classical join cell \(\bigcap_{l<n}\sigma^{-l}c^{-1}(f_l)\). Feeding these into
  the correlation entries and using that \(\rho_\mu\) is diagonal, the off-diagonal entries vanish
  (two distinct words disagree in some slot, forcing an orthogonal pair of indicators) and the
  \((f,f)\) entry is the mass \(\mu(\bigcap_{l<n}\sigma^{-l}c^{-1}(f_l))\) of the join cell. The
  correlation matrix is therefore \(\operatorname{diag}\) of the join distribution, so by
  \(S(\operatorname{diag}p)=-\sum_j p_j\log p_j\) its von Neumann entropy is the Shannon entropy of the
  join --- the classical join entropy at resolution \(n\).
\end{proof}

n33886.title: Per-partition equality of entropy rates
n33886.content:
\begin{theorem}[Per-partition equality of entropy rates]\label{cntEntropyPartition_eq_ksEntropyPartition}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.CNT.cntEntropyPartition_eq_ksEntropyPartition}\leanok
  For each projection partition \(\mathrm{projPartition}\,c\), the CNT partition entropy in the
  abelian corner equals the classical Kolmogorov--Sinai partition entropy of the corresponding
  measurable partition \(c^{-1}(\cdot)\):
  \[
    h_{\mathrm{adPerm}\,\sigma}(\rho_\mu,\mathrm{projPartition}\,c)
      \;=\; h_\sigma(\mu, c^{-1}(\cdot)) .
  \]
\end{theorem}

n33887.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{vonNeumannEntropy_corrMatrix_eq_ksEntropySeq, cntDynamicalEntropy}
  Both sides are the subadditive limit of the same sequence divided by \(n\): the quantum partition
  rate is \(\inf_n S(\mathrm{corrMatrix}\,n)/n\) and the classical partition entropy is the
  corresponding limit of \(H(\bigvee_{l<n}\sigma^{-l}c^{-1})/n\). The per-resolution collapse
  (Theorem~\ref{vonNeumannEntropy_corrMatrix_eq_ksEntropySeq}) identifies the two defining sequences
  term by term, so the limits agree.
\end{proof}

n33888.title: Abelian-corner CNT entropy

n33889.title: Abelian corner \(=\) Kolmogorov--Sinai entropy
n33889.content:
\begin{theorem}[Abelian corner \(=\) Kolmogorov--Sinai entropy]\label{cntDynamicalEntropyAbelian_eq_ksEntropy}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.CNT.cntDynamicalEntropyAbelian_eq_ksEntropy}\leanok
  Suppose every state carries positive mass (\(\mu_i>0\) for all \(i\)). Then the abelian-corner CNT
  dynamical entropy equals the classical Kolmogorov--Sinai entropy of the permutation system:
  \[
    h^{\mathrm{ab}}_{\mathrm{adPerm}\,\sigma}(\rho_\mu)
      \;=\; h_\mu(\sigma) \;=\; \texttt{ksEntropy} .
  \]
\end{theorem}

n33890.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{cntEntropyPartition_eq_ksEntropyPartition, cntDynamicalEntropyAbelian}
  Two inequalities. For \(\le\), each projection partition's rate equals a classical partition
  entropy (Theorem~\ref{cntEntropyPartition_eq_ksEntropyPartition}), which is dominated by the
  classical KS entropy (a supremum over all measurable partitions); take the supremum. For \(\ge\),
  positivity of every \(\mu_i\) forces the cells of any measurable partition \(P\) to be genuinely
  disjoint (not merely a.e.), so \(P\) is realized by an honest cell map \(c\) with
  \(c^{-1}(\cdot)=P\); its projection partition then has the same rate as \(P\), and this rate is one
  of the terms of the abelian supremum. Antisymmetry gives the equality.
\end{proof}

n33891.title: Full CNT entropy dominates KS entropy
n33891.content:
\begin{theorem}[Full CNT entropy dominates KS entropy]\label{ksEntropy_le_cntDynamicalEntropy}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.CNT.ksEntropy_le_cntDynamicalEntropy}\leanok
  Under the same positivity hypothesis, the \emph{full} CNT dynamical entropy of
  \(\mathrm{adPerm}\,\sigma\) in the state \(\rho_\mu\) --- the supremum over \emph{all} operational
  partitions --- dominates the classical Kolmogorov--Sinai entropy:
  \[
    h_\mu(\sigma)\;\le\; h_{\mathrm{adPerm}\,\sigma}(\rho_\mu).
  \]
\end{theorem}

n33892.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{cntDynamicalEntropyAbelian_eq_ksEntropy, cntDynamicalEntropy}
  The abelian dynamical entropy is a supremum over the sub-family of projection partitions, hence is
  \(\le\) the full CNT dynamical entropy taken over all operational partitions. Rewriting the left
  endpoint by the corner equality (Theorem~\ref{cntDynamicalEntropyAbelian_eq_ksEntropy}) turns this
  into the claimed bound.
\end{proof}

n33893.title: Hilbert--Schmidt Gram vectors

n33894.title: Gram factorization of the correlation matrix

n33895.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{gramVec}
  Entrywise this is the trace identity \(\tr\bigl((A\sqrt\rho)^{\dagger}(B\sqrt\rho)\bigr)
  = \tr(\rho\,A^{\dagger}B)\), valid for the Hermitian square root \(\sqrt\rho\)
  (\(\sqrt\rho^{\dagger} = \sqrt\rho\), \(\sqrt\rho\,\sqrt\rho = \rho\)) by trace cyclicity, applied
  with \(A = \mathrm{refine}(g)\), \(B = \mathrm{refine}(f)\): the left side is the \((g,f)\) Gram
  entry \(\langle w_g, w_f\rangle\), the right side is the \((g,f)\) correlation entry.
\end{proof}

n33896.title: Uniform rank bound

n33897.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{corrVal_eq_conjTranspose_mul_self}
  A Gram matrix \(V^{\dagger}V\) has the same rank as \(V\)
  (\(\texttt{rank\_conjTranspose\_mul\_self}\)), and by
  Theorem~\ref{corrVal_eq_conjTranspose_mul_self} the correlation matrix is such a Gram matrix with
  \(V = \mathrm{gramVec}\) having only \(\#(\operatorname{Fin}d\times\operatorname{Fin}d) = d^{2}\) rows; a matrix rank is at
  most its number of rows.
\end{proof}

n33898.title: Uniform entropy bound

n33899.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{rank_corrVal_le}
  Chain the maximum-entropy inequality \(S\le\log(\operatorname{rank})\)
  (Theorem~\ref{vonNeumannEntropy_le_log_rank}) with the uniform rank bound
  \(\operatorname{rank}\le d^{2}\) (Theorem~\ref{rank_corrVal_le}), using monotonicity of \(\log\)
  and positivity of the rank (Lemma~\ref{DensityMatrix.rank_pos}).
\end{proof}

n33900.title: The entropy rate vanishes for every partition

n33901.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{vonNeumannEntropy_corrMatrix_le_log}
  The rate is nonnegative, and by the uniform bound
  (Theorem~\ref{vonNeumannEntropy_corrMatrix_le_log}) each averaged term satisfies
  \(0\le S(\mathrm{corrMatrix}\,n)/n\le\log(d^{2})/n\); since \(\log(d^{2})/n\to 0\), the infimum is
  \(0\).
\end{proof}

n33902.title: The \(\inf\)-rate is a genuine limit

n33904.title: Finite-dimensional CNT dynamical entropy vanishes

n33905.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{cntEntropyPartition_eq_zero}
  Every term of the defining supremum over operational partitions is \(0\)
  (Theorem~\ref{cntEntropyPartition_eq_zero}); the trivial one-cell partition \(x = 1\) witnesses
  nonemptiness at \(k = 1\), so the supremum is \(0\). This is the Alicki--Fannes / Neshveyev--Størmer
  finite-dimensional degeneracy.
\end{proof}

n33906.title: Abelian-corner Fekete subadditivity

n33907.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{vonNeumannEntropy_corrMatrix_eq_ksEntropySeq}
  By the per-resolution diagonal collapse
  (Theorem~\ref{vonNeumannEntropy_corrMatrix_eq_ksEntropySeq}) the sequence coincides term by term
  with the classical iterated-join entropy sequence \(\texttt{ksEntropySeq}\) of the system
  \((\operatorname{Fin}d,\mu,\sigma)\), whose subadditivity is the classical Fekete inequality
  (Theorem~\ref{ksEntropySeq_subadditive}). In the non-commutative case this subadditivity fails ---
  see \S\ref{sec:cnt-counterexample}.
\end{proof}

n33908.title: Abelian-corner Fekete convergence

n33909.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{subadditive_vonNeumannEntropy_corrMatrix_abelian, cntEntropyPartition_eq_ksEntropyPartition}
  Rewriting the rate through the partition-level equality
  (Theorem~\ref{cntEntropyPartition_eq_ksEntropyPartition}) and the diagonal collapse turns the
  averaged sequence into the classical \(\frac1n H(\text{join}_n)\), which converges by Fekete's
  lemma (Theorem~\ref{tendsto_ksEntropySeq}).
\end{proof}

n33917.title: KS entropy \(=\) full CNT dynamical entropy
n33917.content:
\begin{theorem}[KS entropy \(=\) full CNT dynamical entropy]\label{ksEntropy_eq_cntDynamicalEntropy}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.CNT.ksEntropy_eq_cntDynamicalEntropy}\leanok
  \uses{cntDynamicalEntropy_eq_zero, cntDynamicalEntropyAbelian_eq_ksEntropy, ksEntropy_le_cntDynamicalEntropy}
  Under the same positivity hypothesis, the classical Kolmogorov--Sinai entropy of \(\sigma\) equals
  the \emph{full} CNT dynamical entropy --- the supremum over \emph{all} operational partitions, not
  merely the diagonal ones:
  \[
    h_\mu(\sigma) \;=\; h_{\mathrm{adPerm}\,\sigma}(\rho_\mu).
  \]
  This upgrades the one-sided bound Theorem~\ref{ksEntropy_le_cntDynamicalEntropy} to an equality.
  Both sides are \(0\): the KS entropy of a finite-set permutation, and (by
  Theorem~\ref{cntDynamicalEntropy_eq_zero}) the finite-dimensional CNT dynamical entropy --- so the
  equality, while honest, is degenerate.
\end{theorem}

n33919.title: Resolution \(1\): zero entropy

n33920.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  Since \(\Phi = \mathrm{id}\), the depth-\(1\) refinement along \(f\) is just \(x_{f(0)}\); the
  \(\rho\)-weighted pairing \(\tr(\rho\,x_g^{\dagger}x_f)\) reads off column \(0\) of the pure state,
  giving \(\operatorname{diag}(1,0)\) on the classical index. A pure classical distribution has
  Shannon entropy \(0\).
\end{proof}

n33921.title: Resolution \(2\): positive entropy

n33922.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{vonNeumannEntropy_pos_of_sq_ne}
  The depth-\(2\) refinement along \(f\) is \(x_{f(0)}x_{f(1)}\); computing the \((w_{00},w_{00})\)
  entry of \(M^{2}\) against \(M\) gives \(3/8\) versus \(1/2\), so \(M^{2}\ne M\). Strict positivity
  of the entropy for a non-idempotent state (Theorem~\ref{vonNeumannEntropy_pos_of_sq_ne}) then
  yields \(S(\rho[X^{(2)}]) > 0\).
\end{proof}

n33923.title: The CNT entropy sequence is not subadditive
n33923.content:
\begin{theorem}[The CNT entropy sequence is not subadditive]\label{not_subadditive_cnt_entropySeq}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.CNT.not_subadditive_cnt_entropySeq}\leanok
  \uses{entropy_corrMatrix_one_eq_zero, entropy_corrMatrix_two_pos}
  The CNT/ALF entropy sequence \(n\mapsto S(\rho[X^{(n)}])\) of the partition above, under the
  identity dynamics and the invariant pure state, is \emph{not} subadditive: it violates
  \(u_2\le u_1 + u_1\), since
  \[
    S(\rho[X^{(2)}]) \;>\; 0 \;=\; 2\,S(\rho[X^{(1)}]).
  \]
  This is a feature, not a defect: it is precisely why the CNT rate is an infimum (an \(\texttt{sInf}\)),
  not a Fekete limit of a subadditive sequence.
\end{theorem}

n33929.title: Strictly above every abelian restriction
n33929.content:
\begin{theorem}[Strictly above every abelian restriction]\label{cex_strictly_above_abelian}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.CNT.cex_strictly_above_abelian}\leanok
  \uses{corrMatrix, vonNeumannEntropy_eq_zero_of_sq_eq, entropy_corrMatrix_two_pos, cntDynamicalEntropy_eq_zero}
  For \emph{every} abelian (diagonal) operational partition the correlation density matrix is a
  rank-one idempotent at every resolution \(n\) --- a Gram collapse onto the column-\(0\) diagonal
  entry --- so its von Neumann entropy is \(0\)
  (\lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.CNT.cex_abelian_restriction_entropy_zero}); while for the
  non-commuting partition \(\operatorname{cexPartition}\) the length-\(2\) correlation matrix is not
  idempotent, so its entropy is strictly positive. This is issue \#59's ``entropy strictly above every
  abelian restriction'', stated honestly at the per-resolution level: the system-level CNT/ALF rate
  is the disclosed \(0 = 0\) of \Cref{cntDynamicalEntropy_eq_zero}, so the non-commutativity lives in
  the per-resolution correlation matrices.
\end{theorem}

n33930.title: No common canonical MASA
n33930.content:
\begin{theorem}[No common canonical MASA]\label{qDynamics_seal_no_common_canonical_masa}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.CNT.qDynamics_seal_no_common_canonical_masa}\leanok
  The seal's diagonal MASA is not dynamics-invariant --- \(U\cdot\operatorname{diag}(1,0)\cdot U^\dagger\)
  has a nonzero \((1,0)\) entry (\lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.CNT.not_preservesDiag_qDynamics})
  --- and the dynamics' MASA (the eigenbasis, \(=\) commutant of the eigenprojection
  \(\operatorname{eigProj}\)) is not seal-invariant: the dephasing map moves \(\operatorname{eigProj}\)
  out of that MASA, \(E(\operatorname{eigProj})\) failing to commute with \(\operatorname{eigProj}\)
  (\lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.CNT.dephase_eigProj_not_commute}).
\end{theorem}

n33931.title: Reservoir cap in \(2\log d\) form
n33931.content:
\begin{theorem}[Reservoir cap in \(2\log d\) form]\label{cntCumulativeEntropy_le_reservoir}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.CNT.cntCumulativeEntropy_le_reservoir}\leanok
  \uses{vonNeumannEntropy_corrMatrix_le_log, corrMatrix}
  For every unital \(*\)-endomorphism \(\Phi\), state \(\rho\), operational partition \(X\), and
  resolution \(n\), the correlation entropy obeys the uniform-in-\(n\) reservoir ceiling
  \[
    S\bigl(\mathrm{corrMatrix}\,\Phi\,\rho\,X\,n\bigr) \;\le\; 2\,\log d .
  \]
  The reservoir is \(\log(d^{2}) = 2\log d\), \emph{not} the naive single-copy ceiling \(\log d\): the
  correlation-matrix construction lives on a \(d^{2}\)-dimensional Gram factorization, so the honest
  cap is \(\log(d^{2})\).
\end{theorem}

n33933.title: The correlation-entropy sequence is bounded

n33935.title: Cumulative-bounded \(\Rightarrow\) per-step rate \(\to 0\)
n33935.content:
\begin{theorem}[Cumulative-bounded \(\Rightarrow\) per-step rate \(\to 0\)]\label{rate_to_zero_of_cumulative_bounded}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.rate_to_zero_of_cumulative_bounded}\leanok
  Let \(a:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{R}\) be nonnegative and uniformly bounded above by a fixed constant \(C\)
  (a \emph{reservoir}). Then the per-step rate vanishes,
  \[
    \frac{a(n)}{n} \;\longrightarrow\; 0 .
  \]
\end{theorem}

n33955.title: The strict drop survives the block tensoring
n33955.content:
\begin{theorem}[The strict drop survives the block tensoring]\label{relEntropy_strict_drop_dephasing_kron}
  \lean{ErgodicTheory.OperatorEntropy.relEntropy_strict_drop_dephasing_kron}\leanok
  \uses{dephaseKronId, relEntropy_maximallyMixed}
  For a faithful block state \(\beta\) and the reference \(\sigma = \operatorname{diagState} s\)
  (\(0 < s < 1\)), partial dephasing of \(\rho_r\otimes\beta\) against
  \(\operatorname{diagState} s\otimes\beta\) strictly lowers the Umegaki relative entropy:
  \[
    S\bigl((\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})(\rho_r\otimes\beta)\,\big\|\,(\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})(\sigma\otimes\beta)\bigr)
      \;<\; S\bigl(\rho_r\otimes\beta\,\big\|\,\sigma\otimes\beta\bigr).
  \]
\end{theorem}

n33956.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{dephaseKronId}
  The block \(\beta\) is a common faithful ancilla, so the relative entropy is unchanged by it
  (ancilla invariance); the channel factorises on product states, reducing the claim to the
  qubit-level strict drop \(\log 2 - h_2\!\big((1+r)/2\big) > 0\) (the strict maximum of the binary
  entropy at \(1/2\)), which carries through. The reference pair has \emph{distinct} dephasing images
  (\((I/2)\otimes\beta \ne \operatorname{diagState} s\otimes\beta\)), so the pair is non-degenerate.
\end{proof}

n33957.title: No Stinespring recovery, uniform in the block

n33958.content:
\begin{proof}\leanok
  \uses{relEntropy_strict_drop_dephasing_kron}
  The strict relative-entropy drop (Theorem~\ref{relEntropy_strict_drop_dephasing_kron}) is uniform in
  the block; a Stinespring section simultaneously recovering both states would saturate the
  data-processing inequality, contradicting the strict drop (Petz's equality theorem). ``Uniform in
  \(n\)'' means the block \(\mathrm{blk}\) is arbitrary, and the recovery is quantified over
  \emph{all} faithful-ancilla Stinespring dilations on the enlarged system.
\end{proof}
